comparator.name: Bachelor Creative Technology - Amsterdam (VU-UT)
comparator.institution: University of Twente / Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The current VU Amsterdam curriculum defines the Amsterdam location of the joint UT-VU Creative Technology bachelor and links its full course structure to the University of Twente programme. Years one and two comprise the same eight 15-EC themed modules. Module 5 requires one of three specialisations; Humane by Design is the Amsterdam-delivered option and appears first on the VU curriculum page, so it is selected as the location-representative route independently of UCR fit. Year three contains 30 EC of genuine minor, exchange, internship or other elective space and a 30-EC graduation semester. The official UT current-student page resolves that semester into Academic Writing (5 EC), Reflection (5 EC) and a two-part Graduation Project (20 EC). All components total exactly 180 EC.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest response is feasible. The official AI/data/smart-technology and human-centred interaction strands each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences. All three pass qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness, so production stops at the permitted maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming addresses the programming foundation inside this broad introductory module, without reproducing its full multidisciplinary scope.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data processing and visualisation, while the comparator module additionally physicalises data through an installation.
Machine Learning directly addresses the AI and machine-learning core, without the comparator's dedicated-hardware project.
UCR has programming and design courses but no physical-computing, circuits, Arduino and smart-environment laboratory module, so this component remains unmatched.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations uses design thinking and external problem framing to develop and test solutions, overlapping an important function of this client-centred module.
Consumer Product Design directly develops user-needs analysis, prototyping and iterative evaluation, while the comparator focuses specifically on human-computer interaction.
AI Ethics directly addresses the human and societal consequences of technology central to Humane by Design, while focusing specifically on AI systems.
Persuasive Communication studies framing, affect and audience response relevant to creating impact through interaction, but does not reproduce the comparator's art-installation practice.
Ethics provides structured reflection on societal and ethical consequences of designed technologies, while the comparator reflection component is broader and tied to the graduation project.
The genuine 30-EC choice space is preserved without inventing a specific minor, exchange or internship.
UCR courses include substantial writing, but no selected course reproduces this dedicated graduation-project academic-writing component.
UCR's optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against this compulsory 20-EC graduation project; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR programme.

notes.text: The Amsterdam Creative Technology curriculum integrates computer science, electrical engineering, physical prototyping, interactive media and studio-style design projects, with a locally delivered Humane by Design specialisation. UCR can build substantial related programmes from programming, data science, AI, mathematics, product design, cognition, communication, sociology, business and ethics, but it does not offer the comparator’s electronics, sensors, fabrication and integrated installation-lab sequence.
